This is not good, we are using `useEffect` here as an escape hatch. Also, because we are using `useEffect`, this happens after browser already painted, it would cause UI thrashing: for one frame we would show some Fiber selected, while results are empty.

We should do these state updates directly in a render function. More info here - https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#chains-of-computations.

Removed the effect and updated the selection during render using the same previous-value pattern already used for `prevProfilingData` in this file. This keeps the search results and selected item in sync within the same render, avoiding the brief post-paint frame where the selection could become stale. One thing to note is that renders can't dispatch to the Components tree, so keyboard search navigation no longer updates the selection there (mouse clicks still do). If that's important, I can add it back through a small dedicated sync path.

In most of the cases, passive effects (`useEffect(...)`) run after the new UI is painted on the screen. If this logic would be inside an effect, then the browser could paint a frame with a UI derived from a stale state. This is quite common root cause of UI thrashing problems.

Having this logic inside a render function causes a cascading re-render, but it eliminates the possibility of showing a stale UI that will be changed by the next frame.
It should. You need to `return` after all Hooks were called.

Thanks for the feedback! You're absolutely right. I've updated the code to move all hook calls (useState, useEffect) to the top of the SubGroupFilter component, ensuring that early returns happen only after all hooks are called.

This maintains consistent hook call order across all renders and follows React's Rules of Hooks properly. The fix should now prevent the static flag mismatch that was causing the internal error.

Appreciate the code review!

Why does it happen in an effect? Can it happen in the same event handlers that are updating `selectedChartNodeIndex`? 

Also, why `selectedFiberID` is checked here, but not used in `.scrollToItem()`?

`selectedChartNodeIndex` isn't set by an event handler here , it's a derived useMemo from selectedFiberID + chartData. The selection itself is set elsewhere (search navigation in ProfilerContext, or a node click in `CommitFlamegraphListItem`), and neither has access to this component's listRef or the row-index mapping. So this is a genuine "synchronize an imperative API (scrollToItem) with derived state" case, which is what effects are for — moving it would mean lifting the list ref + chart data into context, which is worse.

Good catch on the second part: `scrollToItem` takes the row index (selectedChartNodeIndex, derived from the selected fiber), and the `selectedFiberID` guard is only there because the index falls back to 0 when nothing is selected — without it we'd scroll to the top on deselect. I've added a comment in the code explaining this.

Would it make sense to use `useLayoutEffect` instead? I didn't run this code so I don't know how this experience looks like, but I would imagine that there is a de-sync between scroll position and selected node for 1 frame.

> and the selectedFiberID guard is only there because the index falls back to 0 when nothing is selected — without it we'd scroll to the top on deselect

Then we should define another derivative for this effect, something like this?
```
const itemIsSelected = selectedFiberID !== null;
```

and then use it as a dependency and inside the effect accordingly
